heading: Start with the experience you want
intro: Picture the part of the journey you would most like to remember: a quiet river outing, time to watch birds, a forest walk or an introduction to the region. Choose a few priorities before comparing accommodation. Share what each person enjoys, the dates you can travel and how this stay fits into the rest of your Ecuador journey.
points: Name your two or three main interests.
Separate fixed dates from flexible ones.
Explain your group’s preferred pace and experience.

heading: Choose one regional base
intro: Use the regional guides to create a shortlist, then ask for the exact location of the proposed accommodation and outings. Cuyabeno, Yasuní and the Napo corridor, Tena, Misahuallí and Puyo are starting points for comparison. A destination label does not establish the facilities or activities of a particular property. Compare the proposed stay as a whole rather than adding distant places for their names alone.
points: Request a map or precise location of the base.
Ask where the proposed excursions take place.
Compare the journey from your actual starting point.

heading: Count the time you can enjoy
intro: Put arrival and departure beside the activity program. A three-, four- or five-day description needs a day-by-day explanation before you can compare it with another proposal. Count accommodation nights separately from full excursion days, and notice where transfers leave only part of a day. Keep space for your own pace rather than filling the schedule solely to increase the number of listed activities.
points: Mark transfer periods and planned outings on each day.
Check the number of nights included.
Discuss rest time and any onward connection.

heading: Match the stay to your group
intro: A photograph of a room cannot answer every practical question. Ask about the room arrangement, bathrooms, meals, power and communications that matter to your group, without assuming those facilities are included. Discuss guiding language, group size and the demands of the proposed outings. Explain mobility or dietary requirements early enough for the provider to give a specific answer before you accept the proposal.
points: Ask for the actual room and meal arrangements.
Confirm guiding language and shared or private activities.
Request a clear explanation of terrain and boarding.

heading: Compare the complete quote
intro: Read the price alongside the program it covers. List accommodation, meals, guiding, outings, transfers and equipment, then mark anything optional or paid separately. If two proposals use the same destination name, their scope may still differ. An unclear inclusion is a question to resolve in writing, not a benefit to assume. Keep the quotation and itinerary together so later changes are easy to trace.
points: Confirm the total price for your group and dates.
Identify exclusions, optional activities and payment stages.
Ask who is responsible for each transfer and outing.

heading: Review before you commit
intro: Read the latest official advice for every gateway and route as well as the destination itself. Ask how the provider communicates itinerary changes and what the written cancellation or modification terms say. Keep unresolved questions visible instead of treating silence as confirmation. When the proposal reflects your priorities, request the final version with dates, contacts and the arrangements you have agreed.
points: Review the proposed route against current official advice.
Clarify change terms and the contact for questions.
Save the dated proposal and confirmed arrangements.
